App monitor: leave the scheme's default port out of the check URL (#2209)

Refs #2209 (follow-up of #2210).

## Bug
The http/https app monitor called `https://<host>:443/`, so the request's Host header was `<host>:443`. A virtual-host gateway routing on the host name (HAProxy `hdr(host) -i name`) matches no rule and answers **503**. Found on preprod: the two monitor-only apps on two web services behind such a gateway were Failed with APPERR002 (503), while a plain curl from the same container got 200. The regtest could not see it: its test server does not route on the host name.

## Fix
`appMonitorHTTPRoute` leaves the port out of the URL when it is the scheme's default (443 for https, 80 for http), as a browser does. Any other port stays. `https-cert` still dials `host:443` for the certificate.

## Replication links (T27)
None touched.

## Tests
- Unit: URL per mode and port (443/80 left out, 8443 and http-on-443 kept); Host header on a non-default port; existing probe and certificate tests. `go test -run 'TestAppMonitorHTTPRoute|TestAppMonitorHostHeader|TestProbeNoRoute|TestCert' ./cluster/` ok.
- Preprod: deployed to the active, the two monitors checked against the real services (result in a comment).

fix: keep a later Claude model name as an override on the global page

#2623 made the settings edit check skip a later Claude model name, such as `model: claude-opus-4`, for tools that cannot load it. It did that on the global page too, but `sync --global` (`globalSettingsFor`) writes that name to `~/.codex/config.toml` as is.

So on `serve --global`, with `a.yaml` setting `model: {codex: gpt-5}` and a later `b.yaml` setting `model: claude-opus-4`, a codex edit to `a.yaml` returned 200 and changed nothing: codex still gets `claude-opus-4`. Before #2623 it returned 400 naming `b.yaml`, which was right.

`SettingsOverride` and `SettingsInEffect` now take `global`, and the skip applies in project scope only. The project page keeps #2623's behavior.

## Decisions worth challenging

- **`SettingsModelOverridden` is not read**, as in #2623. When `outputs.codex.config.model` or the `.codex/config.toml` overlay sets the model, that value wins whatever the specs say, so the edit has no effect either way.
- **The global "What each tool gets" is left as is.** It still skips the Claude name and shows codex taking `gpt-5` from `a.yaml`. That bug was already there before #2623; it is tracked in #2624.

## Verification

- `TestEditField_GlobalLaterClaudeModelNameOverridesCodex`: the global codex edit returns 400 naming `b.yaml`. Without the `global` check it returns 200.
- `TestSettingsOverride_SkipsALaterClaudeModelForToolsThatDropIt` adds a global case.
- #2623's project test `TestEditFieldTarget_LaterClaudeModelDoesNotOverrideCodex` still passes.
- `make ci-local` on b916ebce7: `ci-local: ok`. Run with `AGNOSTIC_AI_TARGET` unset (the session sets it and the OpenCode hook test asserts it is unset) and node 24.22.1 on PATH. JetBrains plugin not run; `editors/jetbrains/` is unchanged.

Related to #2619

fix: Cap generated vHA category value at 63-char label limit

## What problem does this PR solve?

The `metroVHACategoryNameCheck` preflight guardrail was calibrated to Prism
Central's 64-character category-value limit instead of the stricter 63-character
Kubernetes label-value limit.

CAPX names metro vHA categories `k8s-vha-capx-{nutanixCluster}-{metro}-default-{idx}`
and stamps the value onto the Kubernetes Node object as a label (e.g.
`ha-native-site`). A value of exactly 64 characters — for example
`k8s-vha-capx-nkp-management-cluster-rocky-p6fz6-metro0-default-1` — passed both
the preflight check and Prism Central, but was rejected by the Kubernetes API
because label values are limited to 63 characters. That rejection panicked the
Nutanix CSI node driver into `CrashLoopBackOff`, so the node's CSINode object
never got its topology keys, and PVCs scheduled there stayed `Pending`
(`PreBind context deadline exceeded`).

This closes the off-by-one gap by lowering the guardrail to 63 characters, so
the value is rejected at cluster admission with an actionable message rather
than failing silently at runtime.

## Which issue(s) does this PR fix?

Fixes [NCN-118631](https://jira.nutanix.com/browse/NCN-118631)

## How was this change tested?

- Updated `TestMetroVHACategoryNameCheck` boundary cases: exactly 63 characters
  is allowed, 64 characters is rejected with the Kubernetes label-limit message.
- `go test ./pkg/webhook/preflight/nutanix/ -run TestMetroVHACategoryNameCheck`
  passes.

test: define __name in the fake stream script

The release workflow's `screenshots` job timed out waiting for a check row in
the Pipeline checks dialog.

`capture-screenshots.ts` runs under `tsx`, and `tsx` wraps the fake
`EventSource` class in `__name(...)`. Playwright serialises that init script
into the browser, where `__name` isn't defined, so it threw and the page kept
the native `EventSource`. The watch was never posted and the dialog said the
live connection was down. Playwright's own transform adds no `__name`, so the
e2e specs never saw it. The class form arrived in #2981.

The init script now defines `__name` first. I ran the capture script against a
fixture build: it finished and wrote `pipeline-checks-*.png`. I discarded the
locally rendered PNGs; the release job owns those.

Typed `test:` because the diff only touches a test helper and the release-type
hook rejects `fix:` for that.

Closes #2990

fix: stop serve at once with a connection that sent no request

`serve` could take the full 5 second shutdown timeout and fail with "stop the server: context deadline exceeded". This made `TestServe_NoInstalledSkipsTheGlobalOverviewComparison` fail on Linux CI, including on main.

The cause: `http.Server.Shutdown` closes idle connections right away, but it treats a connection that has not sent a request yet as busy until that connection is 5 seconds old. Go's transport can leave such a connection behind. On the test's second `http.Get` it dials a new connection while the first one is going back to the idle pool, uses the first, and keeps the unused one. Browsers open connections ahead of a request in the same way, so Ctrl-C on `serve` with a page open could hit this too.

The server now tracks connections that have not sent a request and closes them from a shutdown hook (`srv.RegisterOnShutdown`), plus any that open after shutdown begins. The hook runs after the server marks itself as shutting down, and the server skips the handler for any request it reads after that point, so closing these connections cannot drop a request that a handler would have served.

## Decisions worth challenging

- **No grace period.** An earlier version waited 100ms before closing a connection that had not sent a request. Review found it could close a connection whose request had just been read while its handler still ran. Closing from the shutdown hook has no such window.
- **A request whose header is still arriving at Ctrl-C gets a dropped connection.** That was already the case before: a test that sends half a request header, stops the server, then sends the rest failed 200/200 on the code before this change.

## Verification

- `TestServeUntilInterrupted_StopsWithAnOpenConnectionThatSentNoRequest`: opens a connection that sends nothing, stops the server, and expects it to stop within 2 seconds. Fails before the fix and passes after.
- Root cause reproduced in review: 1 failure in 1,200 runs of the flaky test under `-race` before the fix (a connection the client dialed but never used, closed at 5.02s); 0 in 1,200 after.
- `go test ./internal/cli -race -run 'TestServeUntilInterrupted|TestServe_NoInstalledSkipsTheGlobalOverviewComparison' -count=50` in Docker (`golang:1.26`, Linux): pass.
- `make ci-local` on 16902e2ed: still running at push time; result follows in a comment.

Closes #2627

--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -6,6 +6,7 @@ Changes by release, following [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0
 
 ### General
 
+- `serve` stops at once on Ctrl-C when a browser or client holds a connection open without sending a request. Before, it could wait 5 seconds and fail with "stop the server: context deadline exceeded" (#2627).
 - A personal per-tool `model` or `effort` map in a settings spec no longer drops the shared single value for the tools it leaves out. Shared `model: sonnet` with personal `model: {codex: gpt-5.5}` now syncs `sonnet` to every other tool, where before they got no model (#2602).
 
 #### Web interface
diff --git a/internal/cli/serve.go b/internal/cli/serve.go
index 19066513f..86eb29edd 100644
--- a/internal/cli/serve.go
+++ b/internal/cli/serve.go
@@ -231,6 +231,7 @@ func serveUntilInterrupted(ctx context.Context, ln net.Listener, handler http.Ha
 	ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(ctx, serveSignals(signal.Ignored)...)
 	defer stop()
 	srv := &http.Server{Handler: handler, ReadHeaderTimeout: 5 * time.Second, ReadTimeout: 10 * time.Second, WriteTimeout: 30 * time.Second, IdleTimeout: 60 * time.Second}
+	srv.RegisterOnShutdown(trackFreshConns(srv).close)
 	served := make(chan error, 1)
 	go func() { served <- srv.Serve(ln) }()
 	select {
@@ -290,3 +291,40 @@ func bufferAPIBody(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
 		next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
 	})
 }
+
+// freshConns are connections that have not sent a request yet.
+// Shutdown waits up to 5 seconds for them, and clients such as browsers
+// and Go's transport open them ahead of a request that may never come.
+// Closing them after shutdown begins drops no request: the server skips
+// the handler for a request it reads once shutdown has begun.
+type freshConns struct {
+	mu      sync.Mutex
+	conns   map[net.Conn]struct{}
+	closing bool
+}
+
+func trackFreshConns(srv *http.Server) *freshConns {
+	f := &freshConns{conns: map[net.Conn]struct{}{}}
+	srv.ConnState = func(c net.Conn, state http.ConnState) {
+		f.mu.Lock()
+		defer f.mu.Unlock()
+		switch {
+		case state != http.StateNew:
+			delete(f.conns, c)
+		case f.closing:
+			_ = c.Close()
+		default:
+			f.conns[c] = struct{}{}
+		}
+	}
+	return f
+}
+
+func (f *freshConns) close() {
+	f.mu.Lock()
+	defer f.mu.Unlock()
+	f.closing = true
+	for c := range f.conns {
+		_ = c.Close()
+	}
+}

```
This stops logging per-input metrics (monitoring.dataset.*) by default,
preventing a mapping explosion: the per-input registry key is the input
id (a UUID for filestream, or an autodiscover id such as
kubernetes-container-logs-<pod>-<hash>), so when a Beat's own logs are
re-ingested each id becomes a new field name and exhausts the index
field limit. Restores the namespaces option that became dead code in
PR #49236; default remains [stats], opt in with [stats, dataset].
```

Staging server chosen only on a staging cluster

## Bug

When a cluster has no staging server, the ProxySQL and HAProxy refreshes (`prx_proxysql.go`, `prx_haproxy.go`) call `SetStandaloneAsStaging()`. It took the first standalone server **whatever `topology-staging` said**, and `SetStagingServer()` writes its host into `Conf.StagingServerHost`, which the config save then persists.

Seen on dev3 (MariaDB 11.8.9, ProxySQL, `topology-staging` off): a forced failover left the old master db1 standalone for a moment; it became the staging server and `staging-server-host = "db1"` appeared in the cluster TOML, while db1 rejoined as a replica. No routing impact while staging is off (both proxies use the staging server only under `topology-staging`), but the runtime fact is saved as configuration: turning staging on later would make that replica the staging proxy's writer.

## Fix

`SetStandaloneAsStaging()` returns nil without `topology-staging`: nothing chosen, nothing saved. With staging on, unchanged (the configured server if standalone, else the first standalone one).

No replication link is stopped, repointed or reset (T27).

## Tests

`TestSetStandaloneAsStaging` (off: no choice, no staging-server-host; on: first standalone chosen and saved); `go test ./cluster/ -run Staging` OK.

A value already saved (like dev3's) stays until changed: there is no API setting for `staging-server-host` today.

Cloud18 quote: pool fields read one by one, older-infrastructure and APU-only tests, GUI help (#2212 review)

Follow-up to #2213 (merged), answering its two reviews on ac99ad5dc. Refs #2212.

- **Pool decode** (review points 1 and 2): `cloud18QuoteOf` read the partner's pool through a JSON round-trip with both errors ignored, so a failed decode would have zeroed the whole pool silently. It now reads each field on its own with the quote's `num()` helper, as before #2213: a missing or non-numeric field is 0 and leaves the others. No error path left to ignore.
- **Tests** (points 2 and 3 / missing compatibility case): `TestQuoteOlderInfrastructureWithoutForSale` (no `forSaleDbu`/`forSaleApu`: free pool alone, `forSale` 0/0, no `roomNote`; a string `forSaleDbu` does not zero `freeDbu`), and an APU-only shortfall case in `TestQuoteCountsWhatClustersForSaleGiveBack`.
- **GUI help** (points 3/4 and status cache): off, this instance publishes 0 for sale whatever its offers hold; the creation check follows a change at once, the published status within `cloud18-self-service-cache-seconds`.
- **Doc**: the tests line wrapped, the field-by-field read described.

Answered without change:
- User doc (T8): on docs.signal18.io master (6a305b1), registration page, self-service section and variables table.
- The quote does not know `can-borrow`: left for later, as written in #2212.
- `config.go` re-alignment: gofmt.
- `roomNote` in English: read by MCP and the sales assistant.

Tests: `go test ./server/ -run 'TestQuote|TestSelfServicePoolGate'` passes on the laptop, `go build ./...` clean, JSX parsed. T13: marketplace quote, no regtest; live check after deploy.
